chunks: Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr ibn Abī al-Miqdām narrated from ʿAmmār al-Sābāṭī, who said:
I said to Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام: A man engages in trade, but if he hires himself out, he is given more than what he earns in his trade.
He عليه السلام said: He should not hire himself out, but rather seek sustenance from Allah, the Exalted, and trade; for when he hires himself out, he restricts sustenance for himself.

key_terms.آجَرَ نَفْسَهُ: hires himself out for labor or service in return for wages
key_terms.الرِّزْقَ: sustenance or provision apportioned by Allah
key_terms.يَتَّجِرُ: engages in trade as a means of livelihood

ai.seo_question: Should a person leave trade to hire himself out for higher wages?
ai.summary: This hadith reports a ruling and guidance concerning livelihood, preferring independent trade over hiring oneself out for wages in the case described. The Imam عليه السلام directs the man to seek sustenance from Allah تعالى through trade, stating that hiring himself out would restrict his rizq.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3656 - Muhammad bin Amr bin Abi Al-Miqdam narrated from Ammar Al-Sabati, who said:
I asked Abu Abdullah (as), about a man who trades but, if he hires himself out, earns more than he does in his trade.
Imam (as) said: 'He should not hire himself out but rather seek sustenance from Allah (swt), the Exalted, and continue trading. For if he hires himself out, he will restrict his sustenance.'
